claims.text: Integrating in situ real-time monitoring into SPS enables fine-tuning of the pulsed-current profile and dwell time.
Fine-tuning SPS current profiles and dwell times through real-time monitoring reduces the sintering temperature required for densification.
In situ-controlled SPS can preserve an optimal microstructure while reducing the sintering temperature.
The target powder-based ceramic or alloy conventionally requires high-temperature sintering for densification.
Real-time sensor measurements can capture densification kinetics during SPS.
Densification data acquired in real time can be used to adjust SPS pulsed-current parameters dynamically.
Dynamic SPS control enhances control over grain-boundary formation and diffusion during rapid heating.
Enhanced control over grain-boundary formation and diffusion produces a finer and more homogeneous microstructure.
Optimization of current-pulse profiles and dwell times accelerates diffusion-controlled densification at lower temperatures.
Optimization of current-pulse profiles and dwell times minimizes excessive grain growth.
In situ-controlled SPS will achieve full densification at a lower temperature than conventional SPS without in situ control.
In situ-controlled SPS will preserve or improve microstructural quality relative to conventional SPS.
Conventional SPS without in situ monitoring requires higher sintering temperatures to achieve full densification.
Conventional SPS without in situ monitoring requires longer dwell times to achieve full densification.
The effectiveness of in situ-controlled SPS may depend on powder homogeneity and sensor resolution.
